finding.R1.fp: It may be a newly issued company device. If so, register it as a company device.
finding.R1.sentence: {time}, a USB storage device ({device}) was connected to this PC for the first time.
finding.R1.title: New storage device
finding.R2.fp: It may be legitimate overtime or weekend work.
finding.R2.sentence: {time}, a storage device ({device}) was connected outside business hours.
finding.R2.title: Storage device used after hours
finding.R3.fp: This shows files were opened, not that they were copied. It may be a normal work transfer.
finding.R3.sentence: {time}, {count} file(s) on removable storage{device_part} were opened.
finding.R3.title: Files opened from removable storage
finding.R4.sentence: Starting {time}, {count} files were moved to the Recycle Bin within {minutes} minutes.
finding.R4.title: Many files deleted in a short time
finding.R5.fp: It may be maintenance, but it can also hide activity, so it needs review.
finding.R5.title: Event log cleared
finding.R6.fp: It may have been a correction. Clock changes make other timestamps less reliable.
finding.R6.sentence: {time}, a user account{account_part} changed the PC clock by {minutes} minutes.
finding.R6.title: Clock changed by a person
finding.R7.fp: It may have been charging only. Portable devices leave little record of file transfers.
finding.R7.title: Phone or portable device connected
finding.R8.fp: It may be work use. This tool cannot tell whether files were uploaded.
finding.R8.sentence: There were {count} visits to cloud storage, webmail or file transfer sites ({sites}).
finding.R8.title: Cloud storage or webmail use
gloss.1: Volume serial: a number set when a drive is formatted; it links opened files to a device.
gloss.2: Shortcut record: Windows creates it automatically when a file is opened.
gloss.3: Event log: Windows' time-ordered record of important events.
gloss.4: Integrity value (SHA-256): changes if even one byte of the file changes.
grade.desc.caution: Some records are worth a look. Check the items below.
grade.desc.nothing: No activity needing review was found in the records analyzed. This does not rule out activity that leaves no record.
grade.desc.review: Some records need review. We recommend checking them and, if needed, consulting a security professional.
grade.desc.undetermined: Essential data could not be read. Run the check again with administrator rights.
limit.1: Not court evidence. Expert review is needed to confirm results.
limit.2: No record does not mean no activity.
limit.3: See the README validation status for coverage on real USB devices and client Windows 10/11.
next.device: Check whether the connected devices are company devices and register them if so.
next.keep: Keep the evidence files saved with this report.
next.rerun_admin: Run the check again with administrator rights.
next.review: Have someone check the 'needs review' items and, if needed, consult a security professional.

ui.help.steps:
1. Click 'Check this PC'.
2. Confirm the customer and reviewer and tick 'I am authorized'.
3. Click 'Start check' and wait (usually 1–3 minutes).
4. Click 'Open report'. You can print it or save it as PDF.

ui.welcome.2: It is for first-pass review and is not court evidence.
